newsitem.title: NORWAY: Blue chips fall to drag down Oslo Bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips fall to drag down Oslo Bourse index.

text.p: Norwegian shares traded in negative territory on Wednesday with blue chips falling amid uncertainty in the market, dealers said.
The Total index closed 1.32 percent lower at 1,087.61 points. Turnover was brisk at 1.3 billion crowns, of which 444 million were traded in industrial giant Norsk Hydro.
Hydro closed seven crowns, or two percent, lower at 336 crowns. The share has plunged 42.50 crowns since the company, released disappointing 1996 profits on Monday.
"There is a greater uncertainty in the market following the poor results of Hydro and other big companies," one broker said.
The downturn was also in line with subdued trading at big stock exchanges in Europe ahead of a speech by Federal Reserve chief Alan Greenspan.
Aker Maritime closed 14 percent, or 18 crowns, lower at 107 crowns. The offshore company said after releasing 1996 profits that it would have to work hard to live up to market expectations this year.
Industrial group Kvaerner's A share fell 2.5 percent, or 8.50 crowns, to finish at 335 crowns the day after the release of annual profits that fell short of expectations.
